problem: Whole-body mobile manipulation for household tasks is hard because high-DoF robots (dual arms, torso, omnidirectional base) are difficult to teleoperate at scale and existing policies flatten the action space, ignoring embodiment hierarchy so base/torso errors amplify at the end-effector.
motivation: Analysis of BEHAVIOR-1K shows household tasks need bimanual coordination, stable navigation and extensive end-effector reachability, which need whole-body hardware. Such systems make data collection and coordinated action modelling hard, so a full stack of hardware, interface and algorithm is needed.
key_idea: Pair a low-cost kinematic-twin-arm whole-body teleoperation interface (JoyLo) with WB-VIMA, a transformer policy that autoregressively decodes base, then torso, then arm actions with diffusion heads and fuses colored point clouds and proprioception via self-attention.
insight: Both components matter: on real tasks, removing autoregressive whole-body decoding drops success by up to 53%, and removing multi-modal attention makes the policy overfit to proprioception and ignore vision (4 collisions in lay clothes out). Baselines that predict flattened 21-DoF actions (DP3, RGB-DP, ACT) suffer compounding drift and fail end-to-end. In the user study, JoyLo's direct joint mapping gives higher success, faster completion and lower singularity than IK-based VR/Apple Vision Pro interfaces.
method: JoyLo interface: 3D-printed kinematic-twin arms with Dynamixel motors and Joy-Cons; thumbsticks control base velocity, waist/hip and torso height, triggers control grippers; cost under $500.
Bilateral haptic feedback: torque on JoyLo arms from a PD term on the robot-vs-JoyLo joint difference, giving resistance on contact without force sensors.

Autoregressive whole-body action decoding: three diffusion UNet heads predict base (3-D), then torso (4-D) conditioned on base, then arms+grippers (14-D) conditioned on both, all from the action readout token.

Multi-modal observation attention: PointNet on fused egocentric colored point cloud (head + wrist RGB-D, 4096 points) and an MLP on proprioception; tokens with action readout token go through causal transformer (2 layers, T_o=2).
Training/deployment: DDPM training with 100 steps, DDIM with 16 steps at inference; 10 Hz policy, 100 Hz controller, asynchronous inference, ~0.02 s latency on RTX 4090.

setting.backbone: WB-VIMA: PointNet + MLP encoders, small causal transformer decoder, UNet diffusion action heads (trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: 98-138 real teleoperated demonstrations per task (100, 103, 98, 138, 122) collected with JoyLo on the Galaxea R1 robot; simulated wiping ablation uses 100,000 cuRobo trajectories
setting.observation: egocentric fused colored point cloud (head + two wrist RGB-D cameras) + proprioception (joint positions, base velocity, gripper widths)
setting.action_space: whole-body 21-DoF: base velocity (3), torso joint positions (4), arm joints + grippers (14); 8-step action chunks
setting.simulator: real world (5 tasks); OmniGibson for user study and wiping ablation

numbers_note: Real-robot manipulation tasks; none of the canonical navigation benchmarks are used. Results are task success rates (not benchmark metrics), so numbers is empty.
results: WB-VIMA reaches an average sub-task success of 88% and average/peak entire-task success of 58%/93% (put items onto shelves 14/15). It achieves 13x and 21x higher end-to-end success than DP3 and RGB-DP, while ACT completes no full task. JoyLo gives 5x higher task success and 23% shorter median completion time than VR controllers in the user study.
limitations: Compounding errors over long-horizon multi-stage tasks reduce end-to-end success.
Point cloud quality is sensitive to lighting and reflective surfaces; policy trained only on R1 robot data with limited scene-level generalization.
Operator's third-person view differs from the robot's camera field of view during data collection.
